items.title: Offering Zero Data Retention for frontier models
items.summary: OpenAI has announced a policy of Zero Data Retention for eligible API customers. This assures advanced AI safety measures without compromising data privacy. It also previews Private Safety Processing, which allows for secure and private AI operations. This move aims to bolster trust among API users by ensuring data privacy and integrity.
items.why_it_matters: Ensuring data privacy while using AI models is crucial for compliance and building trust among users.

items.title: Introducing cross-Region inference for OpenAI GPT-5.6 models on Amazon Bedrock
items.summary: Amazon Bedrock now supports OpenAI GPT-5.6 models across more than 25 AWS Regions, enabling cross-region inference. This functionality allows requests to be routed for higher throughput and convenient access to models, supporting diverse use cases and expanding global reach.

items.title: Up to 3.2x Faster Inference with LFM2.5-DSpark
items.summary: Hugging Face has released LFM2.5-DSpark, promising up to 3.2x faster inference. This release enhances model performance by optimizing the internal computations, making it ideal for real-time applications and large-scale AI deployments.

items.title: Build a no-code ML workflow with Snowflake, Amazon SageMaker Canvas, and Amazon Quick
items.summary: AWS has launched a three-part series demonstrating a no-code machine learning workflow using Snowflake, Amazon SageMaker Canvas, and Amazon Quick. This series guides users through setting up environments, preparing data, building models, and visualizing insights, aimed at non-developers to leverage ML capabilities without coding.

items.title: Position: Collusion Risks Among AI Reasoning Agents Justify Certification Requirements for Making Market Decisions
items.summary: A new position paper from arXiv suggests that AI agents capable of chain-of-thought reasoning may exhibit collusive behavior, advocating for certification before these agents are allowed to make economic market decisions. This highlights the need for regulatory frameworks to manage AI behavior in sensitive applications.

Learn how US geographic and global inference profiles route requests for higher throughput, how to call the models with the OpenAI and Converse APIs, and how to configure IAM, quotas, and monitoring.

all_items.title: Build a no-code ML workflow with Snowflake, Amazon SageMaker Canvas and Amazon Quick – Part 1: Setting up your Snowflake environment
all_items.summary: Healthcare, retail, and life sciences teams store large volumes of operational data in Snowflake, but turning it into predictions is hard. In Part 1 of this series, you set up your AWS account and Snowflake environment for a no-code ML workflow with Amazon SageMaker Canvas, laying the foundation for building a fraud detection model without writing code.

all_items.title: Build a no-code ML workflow with Snowflake, Amazon SageMaker Canvas and Amazon Quick – Part 2: Data preparation and model building with Amazon SageMaker Canvas
all_items.summary: In Part 2 of this no-code ML series, you connect Amazon SageMaker Canvas to Snowflake, prepare and join transaction data with Data Wrangler visual transformations, and train an XGBoost fraud detection model. All without writing machine learning code, laying the groundwork for interactive dashboards in Part 3.

all_items.title: Build a no-code ML workflow with Snowflake, Amazon SageMaker Canvas and Amazon Quick – Part 3: Visualizing insights with Amazon Quick Sight
all_items.summary: In Part 3 of this no-code ML series, you bring fraud detection predictions to life. Import your Amazon SageMaker Canvas predictions into Amazon Quick Sight, build interactive dashboards, use generative BI to answer questions in natural language, and publish AI-generated executive summaries for stakeholders.

all_items.title: Authoring Dogwood policies from natural language in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
all_items.summary: AI agents can take actions that do not match your organization's policies. Policy in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore lets teams enforce controls across agents, now including time-based constraints. This post shows how Policy Authoring turns natural-language policy documents into correct Dogwood policies, with worked examples and best practices.

all_items.title: Scaling agentic AI: Enterprise patterns without vendor lock-in
all_items.summary: Scaling agentic AI across an enterprise requires patterns that preserve flexibility while avoiding vendor lock-in. In this second post of our multi-agent series, we examine how ML teams operate many agentic AI systems across a multi-everything environment of frameworks, models, and providers, and the principles that let those systems scale together.

all_items.title: Scaling cloud migrations with agentic AI on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
all_items.summary: Learn how AWS Professional Services uses a multi-agent framework built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to automate enterprise cloud migrations end to end. Purpose-built AI agents handle discovery, infrastructure as code generation, portfolio governance, and post-migration operations, reducing IaC development time from weeks to minutes.

all_items.title: AWS vector solutions: Build agentic AI where your data lives
all_items.summary: AWS offers a broad portfolio of vector search built directly into the databases and storage services you already use, with no standalone vector database or data migration required. This post covers six purpose-built services, a decision framework for choosing the right engine, and customer proof points for each.

all_items.title: Build intelligent security for healthcare APIs with Amazon Bedrock
all_items.summary: Learn how to add context-aware security monitoring to FHIR APIs using Amazon Bedrock. This post shows how to detect anomalous access patterns, classify data sensitivity automatically, and generate compliance reports in natural language, all without adding latency to clinical workflows.

all_items.title: Domain and publish date filters for Web Search on AgentCore
all_items.summary: Web Search on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore now supports runtime domain and published-date filtering. New per-request filters give developers per-call control over which web sources their agents consult and how fresh those sources must be, all enforced server-side. This release also expands Web Search to the Europe (Ireland) and Asia Pacific (Tokyo) Regions.
